_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-25 · A working session with Sam driving SkyView in a browser while we fixed what he found. He confirmed the Memory Briefing works — and then reading it turned up a real problem: it named Sierra College as the college with bad data when the college was actually Moreno Valley. Sierra is our assistant's name AND a genuine California community college, so that is a false statement about a real institution rather than a slip of wording. We recorded the rule; fixing it in the assistant itself needs Sam's go, because it would change what she says on the public page too. On SkyView: the search was announcing highlighted results while showing none (it zoomed out past the point where the dots are drawn at all), two search boxes became one, course names stopped printing on top of each other, and the map is now what you see first with the subject list as a button on it — which we could only do after making the map usable from a keyboard, which it never was. Underneath all of it we found that the ID used to move a course between groups does not always point at just one course; about 1,800 of them point at more than one. Nobody has ever made a bad move, because nobody has made a move at all yet. Those moves are now refused with the reason rather than guessing.
_status: SkyView is genuinely workable now, and one thing is holding back everything built on top of it: the grouped work surface — the screen that shows a cluster of identities that might be the same course — exists for only 5 of the 159 subjects on the map, about 1% of the corpus. Leading with the map means clicking into somewhere with nothing to open most of the time; the page says so rather than appearing broken. Building it for every subject is the next job, and the way to do it already exists in the code for something else. Everything from today is in PR #1329, open as a draft.

items.text: Open SkyView and drive the flipped view. It now opens on the map instead of the subject list, the search lands where the results actually are, and course names no longer print on top of each other. Density and how the drop target should look are your calls.

Say whether we should add an assistant rule that Sierra (our assistant) and Sierra College (a real college in Rocklin) are never to be confused. We have recorded it as a memory, but a rule would also change what the assistant says on the public page, so it needs your go.

Build the grouped work surface for every subject, not just 5 of 159. It is too big to ship in one file, but the code already loads course descriptions one subject at a time on demand, so the same approach applies.

Work the 73 control numbers that point at two genuinely different courses. They sit at 12 colleges and 93 of the rows are at San Jose City College alone, so it is one conversation more than it is a project.

Apply the college-name fold to the member list. We already wrote down which spellings are duplicates, but only one part of the system reads that list — so a curator currently sees 'CaÃ±ada College' with the accent mangled, and two colleges where there is one.

Clean up the one ESL subject name that is not in the official list. Nine identities sit under 'English as a Second Language (ESL)', which colleges created by typing the whole subject name into the course-subject field. The other three ESL names are all legitimate.
Merge PR #1329 once its checks pass — it carries everything from this session.
